# valueJudgementCE

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of valueJudgementCE is to generate benefit-risk visualizations for the publication “How to visually integrate value judgment with clinical evidence”.

## Installation

You can install the development version of valueJudgementCE from [GitHub](https://github.com/) using the following methods:

### Recommended Installation

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Install using pak (recommended)
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence")
```

### Alternative Installation  

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Install using remotes
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence")
```

## Publication Figures

`dev/generate_publication_plots.R` writes the publication figures to `inst/img/pub/`. The file numbers do not follow the manuscript figure numbers, so use this table to find the file for each figure.

| Manuscript figure | File in `inst/img/pub/` | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Figure 1 – Value tree | Not generated by the package | – |
| Figure 2 – Dot-forest plot | `image01_dotforest` | `create_forest_dot_plot()` |
| Figure 3 – Trade-off plot | `image02_tradeoff` | `tradeoff_utility_plot()` |
| Figure 4 – Predicted scatter plot | `image04_scatter` | `scatter_plot(style = "publication")` |
| Figure 5 – Divergent stacked bar chart | `image05_divergent_stacked_barchart` | `divergent_stacked_barchart()` |
| Figure 6 – Cumulative excess plot | `image06_cumulative_excess` | `cumexcess_incidence_plot()` |
| Figure 7 – Value function types | `image07_value_function_types_comparison` | `compare_value_function_types()` |
| Figure 8 – MCDA comparison (Drug A) | `image08_barplot_mcda_comparison_drug_a` | `create_mcda_barplot_comparison()` |
| Figure 9 – MCDA waterfall | `image09_mcda_waterfall_all_drugs` | `create_mcda_waterfall()` |
| Figure 10 – MCDA benefit-risk map | `image10_mcda_benefit_risk_map` | `create_mcda_brmap()` |
| Figure 11 – MCDA tornado (Drug A) | `image11_tornado` | `mcda_tornado()` |
| Figure 12 – Weight sensitivity, Drugs A-D vs placebo | `image13_weight_sensitivity_drugs` | `mcda_weight_sensitivity(comparator_name = "Placebo")` |

Each figure is saved as `.tiff` (for submission) and `.png`. These files are not used in the manuscript:

- `image03_correlogram` (`create_correlogram()`)
- `image12_weight_sensitivity`: Placebo vs Drug A in Study 1
- `image14_weight_sensitivity_treatments`: all active treatments on one chart

The Drug B-D versions of Figures 8 and 11, and the weight sensitivity charts for the other criteria, are in `inst/img/other/`.

## Figure - Dot-Forest Plot

```{r dot_forest_plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
# Load the package and create the plot
library(valueJudgementCE)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions
fonts <- font_config(7, 5)

# Prepare the data and create the visualization
prepared_data <- prepare_forest_dot_data(effects_table)
result_plot <- create_forest_dot_plot(
  prepared_data,
  outcomes_with_thresholds = list(
    "Primary Efficacy" = 0.10,
    "Secondary Efficacy" = -20,
    "Quality of Life" = 10,
    "Recurring AE" = -0.05,
    "Rare SAE" = -0.07
  ),
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)

# Display the plot
result_plot
```

## Figure - Trade-off Plot

```{r tradeoff_plot, fig.width=5, fig.height=5, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions
fonts <- font_config(5, 5)

effects_table_filtered <- effects_table |>
  dplyr::filter(Outcome %in% c("Recurring AE", "Primary Efficacy"))

tradeoff_utility_plot(
  data = effects_table_filtered,
  benefit = "Primary Efficacy",
  risk = "Recurring AE",
  mab = 0.05,
  mar = 0.45,
  tc_benefit = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45),
  tc_risk = c(0.09, 0.17, 0.24, 0.3, 0.35, 0.39, 0.42, 0.44, 0.45),
  utility_levels = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3),
  chartcolors = colfun()$fig7_colors,
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)
```

## Figure - Divergent Stacked Bar Chart

```{r divergent_stacked_barchart, fig.width=14, fig.height=9, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)
library(cowplot)
library(gtable)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions
fonts <- font_config(14, 9)

# Create both plots
stacked_bar_fig <- stacked_barchart(
  data = comp_outcome,
  chartcolors = colfun()$fig12_colors,
  ylabel = "Study Week",
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)

divergent_stacked_bar_fig <- divergent_stacked_barchart(
  data = comp_outcome,
  chartcolors = colfun()$fig12_colors,
  favcat = c(
    "Benefit larger than threshold, with AE",
    "Benefit larger than threshold, w/o AE"
  ),
  unfavcat = c(
    "Withdrew",
    "Benefit less than threshold, w/o AE",
    "Benefit less than threshold, with AE"
  ),
  ylabel = "Study Week",
  base_font_size = fonts$p,
  fav_side = "left"
)

# Extract legend using ggplotGrob
stacked_bar_with_legend <- stacked_bar_fig + 
  labs(fill = "Outcome") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.justification = "center",
        legend.box.just = "center",
        legend.title.align = 0.5) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

g <- ggplotGrob(stacked_bar_with_legend)
legend_index <- which(g$layout$name == "guide-box-top")
legend <- g$grobs[[legend_index]]

# Remove legends from both plots and add a single frame around each full plot
stacked_bar_no_legend <- stacked_bar_fig +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.background = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  )
divergent_stacked_bar_no_legend <- divergent_stacked_bar_fig +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.background = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  )

# Combine plots side by side
combined_plots <- plot_grid(
  stacked_bar_no_legend, 
  divergent_stacked_bar_no_legend, 
  ncol = 2
)

# Add legend on top
combined_bar_charts <- plot_grid(
  legend, 
  combined_plots, 
  ncol = 1, 
  rel_heights = c(0.2, 1)
)

combined_bar_charts
```

## Figure - Value Function Types

```{r value_function_types, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions (both axes 0-100, so width = height * 2)
fonts <- font_config(10, 5)

compare_value_function_types(
  benefit_name = "Efficacy",
  benefit_min = 0,
  benefit_max = 100,
  benefit_label = "Response Rate (%)",
  risk_name = "Safety",
  risk_min = 0,
  risk_max = 100,
  risk_label = "Adverse Event Rate (%)",
  power = 2,
  show_titles = FALSE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)
```

## Figure - MCDA Comparison Plot

```{r mcda_barplot, fig.width=16, fig.height=6, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions
fonts <- font_config(16, 6)

clinical_scales <- list(
  `Primary Efficacy` = list(min = 0, max = 1, direction = "increasing"),
  `Secondary Efficacy` = list(min = 0, max = 100, direction = "decreasing"),
  `Quality of Life` = list(min = 0, max = 100, direction = "increasing"),
  `Recurring AE` = list(min = 0, max = 0.5, direction = "decreasing"),
  `Rare SAE` = list(min = 0, max = 0.3, direction = "decreasing")
)

weights <- c(
  `Primary Efficacy` = 0.30, `Secondary Efficacy` = 0.20, `Quality of Life` = 0.10,
  `Recurring AE` = 0.30, `Rare SAE` = 0.10
)

create_mcda_barplot_comparison(
  data = mcda_data,
  study = "Study 1",
  benefit_criteria = c("Primary Efficacy", "Secondary Efficacy", "Quality of Life"),
  risk_criteria = c("Recurring AE", "Rare SAE"),
  comparison_drug = "Drug A",
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales,
  weights = weights,
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)
```

## Figure - MCDA Weight Sensitivity Plot

```{r mcda_weight_sensitivity, fig.width=7, fig.height=7, fig.retina=1, dpi=600, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)

# Configure fonts for plot dimensions
fonts <- font_config(7, 7)

mcda_weight_sensitivity(
  data = mcda_data |> dplyr::filter(Study == "Study 1"),
  weights = weights,
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales,
  criteria = "Rare SAE",
  shading = "hiview",
  base_font_size = fonts$p
)
```

<details>
<summary>Click to learn more</summary>
**About This Plot**

- One-way sensitivity analysis on criterion weights, following Figures 6 and 7 of [Angelis and Phillips (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.14425)
- The weight on one criterion (here Rare SAE) is varied from 0% to 100%; the other weights are rescaled proportionally so all weights still sum to 1
- Each line is a treatment's overall weighted score; the red vertical line marks the current weight
- Open circles mark weights at which the preferred treatment changes
- This figure uses `shading = "hiview"`, which reproduces the shading in the article: the first band and every other band after it are shaded, and nothing is shaded when the preferred treatment never changes
- The default, `shading = "change"`, instead shades the weights at which a different treatment would be preferred than at the current weight, so the unshaded band around the red line shows how far the weight can move before the decision changes; `shading = "none"` turns shading off

**Getting Help**

- Documentation: Use `?mcda_weight_sensitivity` for detailed function help
- Issues: Report bugs at [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence/issues)  
- Discussions: Join discussions at [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/BR-Visualization/value-judgement-clinical-evidence/discussions)
- Contact: Reach out to the package maintainers via GitHub
</details>

<details>
<summary>Click to view sample code</summary>
```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(valueJudgementCE)

# A single criterion, with shading as in Angelis and Phillips (2021)
mcda_weight_sensitivity(
  data = mcda_data |> dplyr::filter(Study == "Study 1"),
  weights = weights,
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales,
  criteria = "Rare SAE",
  shading = "hiview"
)

# Default shading: weights at which the preferred treatment would change
mcda_weight_sensitivity(
  data = mcda_data |> dplyr::filter(Study == "Study 1"),
  weights = weights,
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales,
  criteria = "Recurring AE"
)

# All criteria, one panel each
mcda_weight_sensitivity(
  data = mcda_data |> dplyr::filter(Study == "Study 1"),
  weights = weights,
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales
)

# Drugs A-D on one chart, to compare their sensitivity to weighting; each
# drug is scored as its difference from the placebo in its own study
mcda_weight_sensitivity(
  data = mcda_data,
  weights = weights,
  clinical_scales = clinical_scales,
  comparator_name = "Placebo",
  criteria = "Rare SAE",
  shading = "hiview"
)
```
</details>
